description: The law and ethics that govern computing professionals and the systems they build: IT law, e-commerce, cybercrime, intellectual property, contracts, privacy and Internet governance, data protection regimes compared across Ghana, Europe, the Americas and Southern Africa, the effects of computing on work and wealth, and professional ethics. Taught to the depth of a leading computer ethics and cyberlaw course.
modelledOn: Quinn, Ethics for the Information Age
Baase and Henry, A Gift of Fire: Social, Legal, and Ethical Issues for Computing Technology
ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct; IEEE Code of Ethics
outcomes: Explain the sources and structure of IT law in Ghana and how it interacts with international law.
Identify the legal requirements of e-commerce, electronic contracts, electronic signatures and consumer protection.
Classify ICT crimes and explain the relevant offences, investigation powers and penalties.
Apply intellectual property law to software, data, content and trademarks, including licensing and open source.
Compare data protection regimes (Ghana's Act 843, GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA, POPIA) and design compliant data handling.
Analyse ethical dilemmas in computing with established ethical theories and professional codes.

units.title: Introduction to IT law
topics: Sources of law in Ghana: the Constitution, statutes, common law, customary law; courts and jurisdiction
Why the Internet challenges law: territoriality, anonymity, speed, intermediaries
Key Ghanaian statutes: Electronic Transactions Act 2008 (Act 772), Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843), Cybersecurity Act 2020 (Act 1038), Electronic Communications Act 2008
Regulators: NCA, Data Protection Commission, Cyber Security Authority, NITA

units.title: E-commerce legal issues
topics: Electronic contracts: offer, acceptance, click-wrap and browse-wrap, timing, mistakes, automated agents
Electronic signatures and records; certification authorities; evidential weight
Consumer protection online: disclosure, cooling-off, unfair terms, dispute resolution; payment regulation and mobile money rules
Online marketplaces and intermediary liability; advertising and spam; taxation of digital services (the e-levy debate)

units.title: ICT crime
topics: Categories: unauthorised access, data interference, system interference, misuse of devices, computer-related fraud and forgery, identity theft, child sexual abuse material, cyberstalking, hate speech
Ghana's Cybersecurity Act and the Electronic Transactions Act offences; the Budapest Convention and the Malabo Convention
Investigation powers, interception, digital evidence and admissibility; international cooperation
Case studies: sakawa and romance fraud, SIM-box fraud, mobile-money fraud, ransomware
Cybersecurity obligations on organisations and critical information infrastructure

units.title: Intellectual property
topics: Copyright: subsistence, ownership, duration, infringement, fair use and fair dealing; software and databases as works; Ghana's Copyright Act 2005
Patents and software patents; trade secrets and confidentiality; trademarks and domain names (UDRP)
Licensing: proprietary EULAs, open-source licences (GPL, BSD, Apache) and their obligations; Creative Commons
Digital rights management, piracy, and enforcement; ARIPO and international treaties (Berne, TRIPS)
Ownership of code written by employees, contractors and students; AI-generated works

units.title: IT contracts
topics: Software development, licensing, SaaS and cloud contracts; outsourcing and service level agreements
Key clauses: scope, acceptance, warranties, liability caps, indemnities, IP ownership, termination, dispute resolution
Agile contracts and change control; escrow; government procurement of IT in Ghana
Reading and negotiating a real contract

units.title: Information privacy and Internet governance
topics: Privacy as a right: constitutional and international foundations; surveillance, profiling, facial recognition
Internet governance: ICANN, IETF, ITU, multistakeholder model; net neutrality; Internet shutdowns and content regulation in Africa
Freedom of expression online, defamation, platform liability and content moderation
Lawful interception, data retention and the balance with security

units.title: Data protection and freedom of information
topics: Ghana's Data Protection Act 843: principles, data controllers and processors, registration, data subject rights, the Commission, enforcement
GDPR: lawful bases, consent, rights, DPOs, DPIAs, breach notification, international transfers, fines
CCPA/CPRA, PIPEDA and POPIA compared: scope, rights, enforcement; the African Union data policy framework
Freedom of information: Ghana's Right to Information Act 2019 and access to public records
Designing a compliant system: privacy by design, data minimisation, retention, security, breach response; writing a privacy notice

units.title: Work and wealth
topics: Automation, AI and employment; the gig economy and platform work; telework
The digital divide within Ghana and globally; digital inclusion and accessibility obligations
Wealth concentration, big tech and competition law; data as an asset
Environmental effects: energy, e-waste, and responsible disposal

units.title: Professional ethics and social issues
topics: Ethical theories: utilitarianism, deontology, virtue ethics, social contract; applying them to cases
Professional codes: ACM, IEEE, BCS; whistleblowing, conflicts of interest, competence, honesty
Ethics of AI and algorithms: bias, transparency, accountability, autonomous systems
Case analyses: Therac-25, Volkswagen emissions, Cambridge Analytica, a Ghanaian data breach
Capstone: a policy brief or ethical analysis presented and defended

schedule.title: Legal system and key statutes
schedule.exercise: Draw a map of the Ghanaian sources of law and match five computing problems to the statute and regulator that handle each.

tasks.title: Place four internet disputes in the right court or authority and identify which source of law applies, from a scored scenario
Match ten technology situations to the correct Ghanaian Act and section family, such as electronic transactions, data protection or cybersecurity
Choose the correct regulator and first reporting step for a telecom outage, a data leak and an online fraud, with evidence cited for each

schedule.title: Electronic contracts and signatures
schedule.exercise: Review the terms and conditions of a delivery app and list three clauses you consider unfair, with the reason.

tasks.title: Decide whether a binding contract was formed in three click-wrap and browse-wrap cases and justify each with offer, acceptance and notice
Resolve a dispute where an automated agent accepted a mistaken price, apply contract principles and be scored on the remedy chosen
Assess the evidential weight of an electronic signature and an email chain in a scored scenario, and choose what proof to present

schedule.title: Consumer protection and online commerce
schedule.exercise: Write a short advice note for a small online seller on disclosure, refunds and mobile money rules.

tasks.title: Identify the consumer protection breaches in an online listing from six marked clues and choose the correct remedy for the buyer
Decide platform liability for a counterfeit product sold on a marketplace and choose the notice and takedown steps that satisfy the rubric
Evaluate a proposed digital services tax on mobile payments, weigh effects on users and government, and defend a recommendation

schedule.title: Cybercrime law and investigation
schedule.exercise: Explain how the Cybersecurity Act and the Electronic Transactions Act would apply to a described phishing campaign.

tasks.title: Classify eight incidents into offence categories such as unauthorised access, fraud or identity theft, and cite the evidence for each
Compare how Ghanaian law, the Budapest Convention and the Malabo Convention each treat a cross-border intrusion in a case study
Preserve and present digital evidence in a seized-phone case, choosing steps that keep chain of custody and admissibility, scored by rubric

schedule.title: Fraud cases and organisational duties
schedule.exercise: Write an incident brief for a mobile-money fraud ring, covering victims, offences, evidence and the response by the operator.

tasks.title: Investigate a romance fraud report by ordering evidence, identifying the offences and recommending the reporting route
Respond to a SIM-box fraud case, decide which operator controls and legal steps to take, and be scored on loss reduced and lawful conduct
Lead the response to a ransomware attack on a critical service, balance the payment decision, reporting duties and recovery, and score against the rubric

schedule.title: Copyright, patents and licences
schedule.exercise: Choose the right licence for a student-built health app and explain how that choice affects what others can do with the code.

tasks.title: Decide infringement and fair dealing in four copying scenarios involving software, databases and images under copyright rules
Choose the right protection for a new algorithm, brand name and customer list between patent, trade secret and trademark
Audit a project's dependencies, find a licence clash between GPL and a proprietary release, and choose the fix that keeps it lawful

schedule.title: Digital rights and ownership
schedule.exercise: Write a short opinion on who owns code written by a student intern and by a freelancer, with a clause you would add to each agreement.

tasks.title: Respond to a piracy complaint about a local film streaming site, identify the treaty and statute that apply, and choose the enforcement steps
Settle an ownership dispute over code written by an employee, a contractor and a student, citing the contract terms that decide each
Decide who holds rights in AI-generated content in a case study, weigh the competing positions, and defend a recommended approach

schedule.title: Software contracts
schedule.exercise: Read an annotated software development contract and write a list of five clauses you would negotiate, with replacement wording.

tasks.title: Choose the correct contract form for a SaaS subscription, a bespoke build and an outsourcing deal, and justify each with the risks transferred
Identify risky clauses in a contract on liability cap, indemnity and termination and pick the amendment that protects the client
Negotiate a software contract over several rounds, trading scope, price and service levels, and be scored on outcomes for both sides

schedule.title: Privacy, governance and expression
schedule.exercise: Write a balanced one-page analysis of a proposal to use facial recognition at a public market.

tasks.title: Assess a facial recognition deployment against privacy rights, decide whether it is proportionate, and justify using the rubric
Respond to a government order to shut down social media during an election, weigh rights and security, and score the argument
Judge a defamation claim over a social media post and a platform's moderation decision, citing the elements of the claim and defences

schedule.title: Data protection laws compared
schedule.exercise: Compare how Ghana's Act 843 and the GDPR would handle the same data breach and the same cross-border transfer.

tasks.title: Register a data controller and respond to a data subject access request under Act 843, with steps and deadlines scored
Run a GDPR-style impact assessment for a health app, choose lawful basis and transfer safeguards, and list the risks found
Compare the response to one data breach under Ghanaian, GDPR, POPIA and CCPA rules, and identify the strictest obligation

schedule.title: Information access and compliant design
schedule.exercise: Write a privacy notice for a school results portal in plain language, covering what is collected, why and for how long.

tasks.title: Draft and handle a Right to Information request for a public contract, deciding which parts may be withheld and why
Design data minimisation and retention rules for an e-commerce system and choose which fields to drop, with reasons
Lead the response to a breach in a compliant system, deciding who to notify, what to say and by when, scored against the rubric

schedule.title: Society, work and environment
schedule.exercise: Write a short essay on whether a bank should replace tellers with automation, weighing workers, customers and the bank.

tasks.title: Advise a company on automating a department, balancing efficiency and job loss, and choose a retraining and transition plan
Plan a digital inclusion intervention for a rural district, choose between connectivity, devices and training, and justify with the evidence
Decide how a university should dispose of 200 old computers, comparing e-waste routes for cost, environment and data security

schedule.title: Ethical theories and professional practice
schedule.exercise: Prepare a policy brief on an ethical issue of your choice and a two-minute defence of its recommendation.

tasks.title: Analyse a dilemma about a delivery app's tracking of riders using utilitarian, duty-based and virtue ethics, and compare the conclusions
Decide whether an engineer should blow the whistle on an unsafe release under a professional code, and choose the first steps to take
Analyse a Ghanaian data breach in the style of the Therac-25 case, identify the failures and assign responsibility with a scored report
